title: Combining Denoised Neural Network and Genetic Symbolic Regression for Memory Behavior Modeling via Dynamic Asynchronous Optimization

problem.claim: Memory behavior modeling requires models that provide both predictive accuracy and interpretable cognitive insight.

gap.claim: Knowledge-informed neural networks have had limited use in behavior modeling, while classical memory equations face quantification and interpretability challenges.

contributions.claim: SPsyINN constrains neural-network training with classical memory equations used as knowledge modules.
The approach combines genetic symbolic regression and neural networks through parallel training and a dynamic joint optimization loss for knowledge alignment.
The approach uses proxy-data-mediated asynchronous interaction between the genetic algorithm and neural network, together with neural-network denoising.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On five large-scale real-world memory behavior datasets, the authors report that SPsyINN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predictive accuracy.
The authors report that ablation studies confirm co-evolution capability, improving accuracy while discovering more interpretable memory equations.
The authors report that code has been released.

narrative_sequence.summary: Memory behavior modeling is important in cognitive psychology and education, but traditional and data-driven approaches have limitations in precision, form, interpretability, or cognitive insight.
Knowledge-informed neural networks remain limited in behavior modeling, and classical memory equations are difficult to quantify and interpret.
SPsyINN combines classical memory-equation knowledge modules, genetic symbolic regression, neural networks, parallel training, and dynamic joint optimization.
Asynchronous proxy-data interaction addresses differing optimization methods and hardware requirements, while denoising targets noise robustness and generalization.
The authors report predictive improvements on five real-world datasets and ablation evidence for co-evolution and more interpretable equations.

source_observation.claim: The method aligns a neural model with an evolving symbolic knowledge module through joint optimization and asynchronous proxy-data interaction.

interpretation.claim: Combining differentiable learning with symbolic search may support a tradeoff between predictive performance and interpretability when their interaction is explicitly coordinated.

application.claim: For behavior-modeling tasks with domain equations and mixed optimization regimes, consider coupling neural prediction with symbolic equation search and an explicit communication mechanism.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond memory behavior modeling or which component is necessary for the reported gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, sizes, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or numerical performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the discovered memory equations or the ablation configurations.
The abstract does not provide implementation, computational-cost, or reproducibility details beyond the code-release statement.
